title: 3.1 Law of Sines

icans: I can use the Law of Sines to solve oblique triangles (AAS or ASA).
I can use the Law of Sines to solve oblique triangles (SSA), including the ambiguous case.
I can find the area of an oblique triangle and solve real-life problems.

vocab: two sides and an angle ___________ one of them: there may be no triangle, one, or two
Area = ______________ = ½ab sin C = ½ac sin B

blocks.p: Draw a large triangle with NO right angle. Label it ABC (side a across from angle A, and so on). Measure the sides in centimeters and the angles in degrees.
What do you notice? Compare with another pair.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: When to use it: Use the Law of Sines for ______, ______, and ______.

blocks.stem: Solve the triangle:  C = 102.4°,  B = 28.7°,  b = 27.4 feet. Round to two decimal places.
Solve the triangle:  A = 22°,  a = 12,  b = 5. Round to two decimal places.

notes: The ambiguous case (SSA): In the SSA case, if sin B > 1 there is _______________. If sin B < 1, check whether _______________ also works.

blocks.stem: Show that there is no triangle with A = 85°, a = 15, and b = 25.
Find two triangles with A = 20.5°, a = 12, and b = 31. Round to two decimal places.
Find the area of a triangular lot with sides of 52 meters and 90 meters and an included angle of 102°.
To find the distance from point A to a tree at point C across a river, a surveyor walks 233 meters along the bank from A to B. She measures ∠CAB = 54° and ∠CBA = 76°. Find AC.
Solve the triangle:  A = 40°,  B = 60°,  a = 10. Round to two decimal places.
How many triangles have A = 30°, a = 6, and b = 10? Find B for each.

tickets.stem: A = 35°, B = 70°, a = 8. Find b. Round to two decimal places.
How many triangles have A = 50°, a = 4, and b = 10?
Find the area of a triangle with a = 7, b = 9, and C = 40°. Round to two decimal places.
